rounds.text: Rishiroop Ltd trades at an attractive valuation of 9.51x P/E [E1] and 0.79x price-to-book [E2], representing a steep discount compared to the broader sector benchmarks of 21.43x P/E [E6] and 2.4x P/B [E7]. The company is exceptionally well-capitalized with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and Rs 0 Cr in borrowings [E37, E38], backed by positive free cash flow of Rs 4 Cr [E36]. Recent operating metrics show a powerful inflection, highlighted by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 33% [E17], profit growth of 212% [E21], and an expanding operating margin reaching 13% compared to 9% three years prior [E30]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests the intrinsic value sits at Rs 145 per share against a market price of Rs 129 [E42], while reverse DCF calculations imply that the current market price incorrectly prices in negative earnings growth [E44]. Conceded: the company has delivered weak 5-year sales growth of 5.69% [E52], a low 3-year average return on equity of 7.25% [E53], and inconsistent operating margins over the last two years [E32].

Rishiroop Ltd carries significant fundamental underperformance beneath its headline multiples, highlighted by a multi-year contraction in top-line and bottom-line metrics including a 3-year compounded sales growth of -7% and compounded profit growth of -18% [E16, E20]. Return metrics further undermine the investment thesis, with recent return on equity plunging to a meager 3% and a low 3-year average ROE of 7.25% against a sector benchmark of 11.28% [E9, E29, E53]. Earnings quality is visibly compromised as reported profits heavily outpace cash generation, evidenced by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.57x alongside a concerning note that earnings include Rs. 5.16 Cr in other income [E34, E54]. Conceded: the company trades at a discounted P/E of 9.5x and P/B of 0.79x relative to sector benchmarks, and displays a zero debt-to-equity structure [E6, E7, E37]. However, this apparent cheapness is entirely justified by structurally sluggish long-term growth, with 5-year compounded sales growth limping at 5.69% and 5-year profit growth contracting by 18% [E19, E52].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth is -7% [E16] and 3-year compounded profit growth is -18% [E20]. However, focusing on multi-year contractions ignores the powerful inflection underway in the most recent periods, where trailing twelve-month sales surged by 33% and profits exploded by 212% [E17, E21]. Conceded: median return on equity last year dropped to 3% [E29]. Nevertheless, operating margins are expanding significantly, rising by 4 percentage points in the TTM period to 13% and repeating that 4 percentage point expansion in the most recent September quarter [E30, E31]. Conceded: cash conversion for March 2026 was 0.57x alongside a note of Rs. 5.16 Cr in other income [E34, E54]. Despite this, the company generated tangible positive free cash flow of Rs. 4 Cr and operates with a pristine debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, making it almost debt-free while sitting safely inside a favorable capital goods tailwind [E35, E37, E49, E65].

Conceded: TTM sales surged by 33% and profits exploded by 212% [E17, E21]. However, this short-term surge sits on top of structural stagnation, marked by a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -7% and an 18% profit decline over both 3 and 5 years [E16, E19, E20]. Conceded: operating margins expanded by 4 percentage points in the TTM and September 2026 periods [E30, E31]. Nevertheless, the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly classified as inconsistent over their respective periods [E32, E33], and earnings are artificially padded by Rs. 5.16 Cr in other income [E54]. Conceded: the company generated Rs. 4 Cr of free cash flow and carries a 0.00x debt-to-equity ratio [E35, E37]. Despite this clean balance sheet, cash conversion is a dismal 0.57x because profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation, pointing directly to concerning receivables and accruals [E34].
